known.toggle: What we know about this link
known.title: What our server knows about this link.
known.sub: Printed from what our server answered a moment ago, column by column.
known.id: random; not derived from your file
known.mode: the kind of rule, and where the link is in its life
known.views: the open count of the rule
known.expires: when it leaves on its own, rounded up to the hour
known.wrapped: an encrypted copy of the file key, useless without your link; erased at exit
known.access: a hash of a token your link derives: it lets us check you hold the link without learning it; erased at exit
known.link_hash: a hash of a proof that you hold the link itself, so wrong passwords count only for people who have it
known.kdf: password links only: how your browser stretches the password; never the password
known.retention: files live as long as their links, unless kept in a locker; which pool of space it uses
known.owner: whether a locker owns it. If one does, we store that locker's random id
known.header: format details in clear, so your browser can read the file back
known.header_value: {size} bytes: format version {v}, {n} chunks, random salt
known.meta: your file's name, type and real size, encrypted; we can't read it
known.size: padded, so the exact size stays hidden
known.ct_hash: a hash of the stored ciphertext
known.ip_what: used for this request and for rate limits kept in memory; never written to disk
known.never.name: the file's name, type and real size in readable form
known.never.email: an email address (we never ask for one)
known.stored_what: the file exactly as our disk holds it; this uses no open
known.stored_after: That's what we have. It's noise without the key.
claim.c5: We delete the ciphertext from our disk within a minute of its exit. If the exit was a download, we wait for it to finish (at most {ticket_min} minutes). We keep a note that the link existed for {tombstone_days} days, so we can tell you why it's gone. We never had the key, so any leftover bytes are noise.
claim.c5db: Our database (never files) is backed up daily and each copy is kept {db_backup_days} days. It holds the rows this panel prints.
claim.c5snap: Our host (Hostinger) can take weekly snapshots of the whole server. We haven't switched them off, and we haven't yet confirmed in its panel how long it keeps them. A file that existed when one was taken stays in it, as ciphertext, until that snapshot is rotated out.

upgrade.lede: Free space is a fair share of one real disk. Need more? Rent it in tTARI.

claim.c11_proof: We credit a payment only after the official Tari library opens its commitment to the exact amount and a Tari-run public indexer shows it committed on the chain. A wallet saying “sent” isn't enough.
claim.c11_wallet: We credit a payment only after our wallet sees it and a Tari-run public indexer confirms it exists on the chain. The amount is the one our wallet reads.
verify.title: Receipts
verify.lede: Receipts for the links on this device, each checked in this browser against the root SealLog holds on the Ootle. A check shows that the tree we committed to at that epoch contains your file's ciphertext hash, as this browser computed it when it locked the file, or the record of its exit.
verify.log: This log has no owner, so nobody, us included, can change its rules or the code behind it (template {template}). Only the key {writer} can add checkpoints.
verify.off: Receipts are off on this deployment, so there's nothing to check yet.
verify.untrusted: This SealLog component doesn't show what makes a log trustworthy (no owner, one writer key), so nothing was checked against it.
verify.none: There are no links on this device to check.
verify.ok: included at checkpoint #{index} (epoch {epoch}); the root matches the SealLog component on the Ootle.
verify.bad: the proof doesn't match the root on the Ootle. Please tell us.
verify.pending: not on the record yet; the next checkpoint is around {date}.
